news.title: On this day in space! Nov. 28, 1967: Astronomers Jocelyn Bell and Antony Hewish disover the 1st pulsar with Li
paras: On November 28, 1967, astronomers Jocelyn Bell Burnell and Antony Hewish found the first pulsar. A pulsar is a very dense star that spins quickly. It sends out two beams of light in opposite directions. From Earth, those beams can make the star seem to blink at regular times.

Bell Burnell and Hewish saw the signal blink every 1.33 seconds. They jokingly called it “Little Green Men 1” because they did not know what caused it. Finding more pulsars showed they came from stars, not aliens. Pulsars can act like very accurate clocks, helping scientists study space and guide spacecraft far from Earth.

news.title: 12 grains of dust found high in Earth's atmosphere reveal secrets of water at the edge of the solar system
paras: The dust particles contain mineralogy that has been altered by water containing heavy isotopes of oxygen. And it turns out they hold the secrets of a special kind of 'heavy' water that seems to be surprisingly abundant in the outer solar system.

When analyzed by a team of scientists the 12 dust grains, which were captured by NASA's stratospheric ER-2 research aircraft, show signs of having interacted with a form of water that contains heavy oxygen isotopes. This is important because to better understand how the planets formed, scientists are seeking to understand how various materials were distributed around the early solar system 4.5 billion years ago.

sport.title: November 28, 1999: The day Pete Sampras won the ATP Finals for the fifth time
paras: On November 28, 1999, Pete Sampras beat Andre Agassi in the season-ending tennis finals. He won the event for the fifth time, matching Ivan Lendl’s record. Earlier in the same event, Agassi had beaten Sampras easily. But Sampras won their final match in three sets.

Sampras had missed two major tournaments that year because he was injured. He had also lost his place as the world’s top-ranked player. This victory gave him a strong finish to a difficult year. It also showed Agassi that Sampras could still challenge him in the biggest matches.

sport.title: Rennae Stubbs clarifies her comments about Alexander Zverev not deserving number one
paras: Rennae Stubbs has received backlash for her comments about Alexander Zverev and the number-one ranking. During a recent episode of her podcast, Stubbs said Zverev was number one ‘in name only’ , having finished 2026 ranked ahead of Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner. Several former players criticised Stubbs for what she said, including four-time Grand Slam doubles champion Paul McNamee.

“Well, Rennae [Stubbs], both you & I were number one in doubles. Did that make you better than [Martina] Navratilova, or me better than [John] McEnroe? On the other hand, rankings are objective & [Alexander] Zverev deserved it,” he said.
